title: Advance Economic Indicators Report (advance goods trade, retail & wholesale inventories, Nov 2026 data)
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html lists 'Advance Economic Indicators Report (International Trade, Retail, & Wholesale) | December 28, 2026 | 8:30 AM | November 2026', release code A202612280830 (re-fetched direct 2026-09-05, all 179 rows parsed) - and it is the LAST row on that calendar. CORRECTED 2026-09-05 by this event's initial research: the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx does NOT schedule a 2026-12-28 GDPNow *posting* as this field previously stated. The 12-28 AEIR sits on the workbook's InternalUpdates sheet, whose own note text defines those as 'non-posting dates'; PostedUpdates ends at 2026-12-23. The date corroboration survives - two independent primaries still expect the report that day - but the word 'posting' did not, and the difference is the most consequential fact about this edition. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and because the funding exposure below is precisely a reason not to treat the date as settled
notes: THE FUNDING-EXPOSED EDITION OF THIS SERIES, and the reason it is worth a row rather than the ordinary calendar noise a quarterly successor would be. H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02) funds the government only through 2026-12-11; this release lands 17 days past that cliff. What makes the exposure different from durable-goods-2026-12-23's - the sibling row filed for the same cliff - is the failure mode. On this exact series' measured 2026 precedent Census DELETES rather than delays: the January 2026 and February 2026 reference months still read 'Suspended' on the Census calendar and were never published, while December 2025 data merely slipped 1/28 to 2/19 under a Census bulletin whose own wording is 'delayed due to the recent lapse in federal funding'. Advance durable goods, by contrast, delayed ~27-29 days and lost nothing. So the honest label on this edition is MAY NOT EXIST, not may be late. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's initial research, which REFUTED the clause that used to follow ('a deleted edition is not recoverable information, unlike a late one'): parsing all 179 calendar rows shows that for BOTH suspended reference months the full International Trade report (2026-03-12, 2026-04-02), advance durable goods (2026-03-13, 2026-04-07) and wholesale inventories (2026-03-19, 2026-04-09) all published - and that the December-2025 edition which 'merely slipped' came out 2026-02-19 under release code A202602190830, the SAME date and code as the full trade report it exists to precede, i.e. lead time zero. The AEIR normally leads that report by 6-11 days (median 7, eight clean 2026 reference months). A lapse destroys this report's lead time, not its data; the only other Suspended series on the whole calendar is Preliminary U.S. Imports for Consumption of Steel Products, also a preview - Census cancels previews and keeps reports. The row still earns its place, but for a different reason: the Atlanta Fed files 2026-12-28 as an InternalUpdates (non-posting) date and PostedUpdates ends 2026-12-23, so this edition's composition churn - full strength on the December subsample, 0.586pp median vs 0.048pp, churn-to-headline 3.9x - lands with no public vintage on the day. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside this one: advance-economic-indicators-2026-11-27 (October data), which sits inside the CR window and whose only claim is that a macro print precedes the 12-09 FOMC - the generic argument this calendar's bar rejects; its absence is a decision, not an oversight. Not a tradeable print on its own (symbols: [], no house playbook is macro-keyed). Discovered during the advance-economic-indicators-2026-10-28 initial research (2026-09-05).
